subject: Subscription extension & contract revision — recommended edits for MSA + capacity schedule

Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Subscription extension + capacity bump — contract drafts attached

Hannah,

Thanks for the chat this morning. Per our internal budget and anticipated usage, QuantumPay is looking to: 
- Extend the subscription term from 12 months to 24 months (effective Mar 1)
- Increase committed capacity to 2.5x current baseline (see attached capacity schedule)
- Keep the price step at the committed tier, but add a transitional credit for the ramp month

Attached are the MSA + the updated capacity schedule (QP-Capacity-Schedule-v3.xlsx). We've had our legal team make a few markups in the MSA — mostly around: liability cap, audit notice period, and a short data-residency paragraph. We want to get these in a final package for e-sign this month if possible.

Please let me know if Redwood has concerns with the requested language. Happy to set a call to walk through the redlines.

Thanks,
Elena Ortiz
Head of Cloud Ops | QuantumPay

Elena,

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the attachments. I've looped in Aditya (account exec) and Rishi (legal ops lead) so we can triage the redlines and return a consolidated set of edits. High-level notes after a quick pass:

- Term: 24 months is fine, we just need to confirm renewal auto-renew language (we recommend an opt-out window of 60 days unless you prefer 30).
- Capacity schedule: we can support 2.5x but need a clear burst policy for >4x transient usage and how overage pricing applies during bursts.
- Liability cap: your proposed cap (3x prepaid fees) is above JD team's standard. Rishi, please propose the closest acceptable limit that balances enterprise risk and procurement expectations.
- Audit / SOC2: SOC2 doc attached looks current — we can add a standard audit cooperation clause (30 days notice).

I'll create a redline with inline comments and return by EOD PST. If QuantumPay legal wants to do a joint review, we can set a 30-min slot tomorrow.

Next steps I propose:
1) Redwood returns our consolidated MSA redline (Hannah + Rishi) including a tracked-capacity schedule.
2) Aditya and Elena align on commercial credit for the first month of ramp.
3) Legal-to-legal call (if needed) and finalize e-sign package.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt

Elena / team — quick commercial clarifications from Redwood: 

- Pricing: We'll honor the current committed rate for the extended 24mo term. For the increased committed capacity, we'll apply a one-time pro-rated invoice for the incremental committed units effective Mar 1.
- Ramp credit: We can allocate a 25% credit on the incremental committed spend for the first 30 days of the ramp (applies only to committed units, not overages).
- SLA credits: Given the higher commitment, we can move to a 99.95% availability SLO for the committed capacity with tiered crediting — I'll have legal draft the SLA schedule.
- Migration/Capacity increase timeline: propose staged rollout over 6 weeks to avoid a hot cut.

I've uploaded a draft capacity schedule with proposed billing dates (see attachments). If those dates work for QuantumPay, I'll prepare the commercial addendum to attach to the MSA redline.

Thanks all — quick legal-commercial note from our side. We've had Andrew (c.c.) review the MSA. A couple of counterpoints from QuantumPay legal: 

- Liability cap: We need a higher cap in the event of data breach tied to secured PII exposure. Suggested language: cap does not apply to claims arising from willful misconduct or gross negligence; for breaches, cap = 6 months' fees or actual damages (whichever is higher).
- Audit notice: 30 days may be tight for us. Can we agree to 45 days?
- Data residency: We need a clause guaranteeing that Critical Customer Data for Core Prod region will remain in the US unless otherwise approved.

Andrew, feel free to add specifics. If you can, please flag the exact lines in the redline doc so we can converge quickly.

—James
James Li
Dir, IT Infrastructure | QuantumPay

Hannah / Aditya — copying the specific MSA clauses we want clarified (see inline comments in QP-Renewal-MSA-2027-01-11.docx):

1) Section 10 (Liability): We propose language that preserves a general liability cap but excludes breach/government penalty claims. We are open to a negotiated monetary floor (6 months of committed fees) for security incidents that result in regulatory liability.
2) Section 12 (Termination for convenience): We request a 90-day notice out for the extended term with pro-rated refunds for unused prepaid committed capacity.
3) Data retention & export controls: Our compliance team wants explicit export-control cooperation language.

If Redwood can provide a response to the three points above and accept a 45-day audit notice, QuantumPay will accept the 24mo term and the 2.5x committed capacity as proposed. We'd like to finalize legal language by EOD Friday to meet our procurement window.

Andrew Cole
Senior Counsel | QuantumPay
andrew+legal@quantumpay.com

Team — pulling threads together after the legal asks: 

- Liability cap: Rishi and I reviewed — Redwood can accept an exception for willful misconduct/gross negligence. For security incidents, Redwood agrees to a security carve-out with a monetary floor that will be negotiated; proposed starting point: 4 months' committed fees or actual damages for substantiated regulatory fines (we'll present wording).
- Audit notice: we accept 45 days.
- Termination: we can accommodate a 90-day termination for convenience with pro-rated refunds on prepaid committed capacity provided QuantumPay agrees to a minimum notice of 90 days and a one-time separation fee to cover reserved capacity reallocation (details in the commercial addendum).
- Data residency & export-control language: Redwood will add an explicit statement for Critical Customer Data to remain in the US by default; export control cooperation language will be added to the security addendum.

Action items / timeline:
1) Rishi to deliver consolidated redline (MSA + SLA + capacity schedule) by Fri 2027-01-15 11:00 AM PST.
2) Aditya to draft the commercial addendum with billing schedule & ramp credit details by Fri 2027-01-15 3:00 PM PST.
3) QuantumPay legal to flag any last-line edits by Fri close of business; if granted, Hannah will prepare DocuSign package over the weekend.

If everyone is aligned, please reply with a single-line "ACK" so we can lock the deadlines. I'll also add Marissa (renewals lead) to help coordinate PO processing and billing setup.

Thanks all — looking forward to closing this quickly.

Best,
